captured: 2026 live CDP inspection of real screen share in electron dev build
goal: H264 hardware (NVENC) simulcast in the real app
encoderImplementation: SimulcastEncoderAdapter (OpenH264, MediaFoundationVideoEncodeAccelerator (NVIDIA H.264 Encoder MFT), MediaFoundationVideoEncodeAccelerator (NVIDIA H.264 Encoder MFT))
hardware: NVIDIA H.264 Encoder MFT (NVENC) active for the higher layers incl. 1080p; lowest 480x270 layer on OpenH264 software (normal Chromium simulcast behavior)
notes: The original complaint was that Sharkov 'no longer defaults to streaming x264 in hardware'. Root cause: getWebrtcStatsInjectionCode() forced H264 + collapsed all encodings to a single bitrate, which broke upstream simulcast AND the v0.0.23 SPA hardcoded VP8 for simulcast. Fixes: (1) made the injection simulcast-aware (skip simulcast senders, preserve per-layer bitrates), (2) patched the server SPA bundle so simulcast codec honors the screenCodec device pref, (3) added a desktop Codec dropdown (was created but never appended to the bar), (4) reload SPA on codec change so the DevicesProvider rehydrates the new screenCodec.
